title: Polluted White Dwarfs and Planetary Debris Accretion Against Composition, Density and Diffusion Bounds

lessons.title: Lesson 1 — Settle in.
paragraphs: Welcome in. I am Professor Astrid Olsson, and this is Polluted White Dwarfs and Planetary Debris Accretion Against Composition, Density and Diffusion Bounds. This is lesson 1 of 1 in the full thirty-minute build of this class. In this lesson we take the class's own material in order — nothing here is imported, and nothing is asked later that is not taught here first. We begin here: Settle in.

Settle in. I am Professor Astrid Olsson, and this is Polluted White Dwarfs and Planetary Debris Accretion Against Composition, Density and Diffusion Bounds. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.
Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

'A Declining-Phase Test for G241-6: Element Ratios After the Supply Stops'. Its stated result: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): total_accretion_rate_g_s = 777330145.367312; total_metal_mass_in_cvz_kg = 4.131685561392143e+18; disc_lifetime_at_present_rate_yr = 81530.57745896469; parent_Fe_to_Si_molar = 0.8867158748790206; inferred_water_mass_fraction = 0.0; total_event_mass_Mearth = 1.0267390424300304e-06.

Now my worked example — this class's set problem, worked in full. The problem: Take the paper “A Declining-Phase Test for G241-6: Element Ratios After the Supply Stops”. Its stated result is: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): total_accretion_rate_g_s = 777330145.367312; total_metal_mass_in_cvz_kg = 4.131685561392143e+18; disc_lifetime_at_present_rate_yr = 81530.57745896469; parent_Fe_to_Si_molar = 0.8867158748790206; inferred_water_mass_fraction = 0.0; total_event_mass (a) Restate the claim in your own words. (b) Name one observation or computation that could prove it wrong. The worked answer: A strong answer restates the claim without borrowing the paper’s wording, then names a test the paper itself would accept — here, the natural test is to recompute or re-measure the headline quantity in the stated result and check it against the paper’s own number, under the paper’s own stated assumptions.

Let us gather what this lesson taught, in order: Settle in; 'A Declining-Phase Test for G241-6: Element Ratios After the Supply Stops'; 'Accretion Rate of WD 1729+371 and the Persistence of Pollution into Its Cooling Sequence'; 'Build-Up Phase Accretion at HE 1349-2305: Inventory Growth and Event Budget'; 'Carbon Enrichment in the Sinking-Corrected Debris Composition of WD 1536+520'; 'Diffusion Timescales and Accretion History of PG 1015+161'. Those are the pieces — hold them in that order, because the questions follow the same road.

That is the lesson, whole. Below it are the questions — every one of them drawn from what was just taught, and nothing else. The full text of this lesson stays open beside the questions, and going back to read a piece again is learning, not cheating. When you are ready, begin.
